==Biography==
Ssumday made his professional debut in 2013, competing on [[KT Rolster Bullets]], the sister team of [[KT Rolster Arrows]]. They made their debut in the [[Champions/2013/Spring|Champions 2013 Spring]] tournament, placing 5-8th, ahead of [[KT Rolster Arrows]]. They eventually became the runners-up of the [[Champions/2013/Summer|summer season]]. Ahead of 2014, Ssumday made the switch to [[KT Rolster Arrows]], winning the [[Champions/2014/Summer|Champions 2014 Summer Split]]. Despite their tournament win, handing Ssumday his first title, [[KT Rolster Arrows]] failed to qualify for [[World_Championship/2014|Worlds 2014]], as [[KT Rolster Arrows]] lost 0:3 against [[NaJin White Shield]].

In 2015, the [[KT Rolster]] rosters merged to form just a single roster. Ssumday became their toplaner, but the team failed to make playoffs in the [[LCK/2015/Spring|LCK 2015 Spring season]]. The team managed to qualify for [[World_Championship/2015|Worlds 2015]] in the summer, bringing Ssumday to his first international tournament. [[KT Rolster]] placed top 8, losing against country mates [[KOO Tigers]], who would go on to become 2nd in the tournament. 

Ssumday stuck to [[KT Rolster]] for 2016, placing 3rd and 2nd in the two splits, but eventually falling short in the [[LCK/2016/Regional_Finals|Regional Finals]] with a loss against the eventual world champions [[Samsung Galaxy]]. He would move to North America in the next season, with his last tournament result in Korea being the [[KeSPA_Cup/2016|2016 KeSPA Cup]], in which the team got invited to the playoffs but was immediately eliminated by [[Kongdoo Monster]].

Ssumday became [[Dignitas]]' toplaner in 2017, placing 5-6th in his [[LCS/North_America/2017/Spring|NA LCS Debut season]]. The team made a single change heading into summer, replacing [[Xpecial]] with [[Big]], but was unable to get further than 4th place in both the Summer season and the regional playoffs. Despite that, Ssumday stood out and won the 1st All-Pro Team award. 

With the [[NA LCS]] moving to a franchised format, Ssumday left [[Dignitas]] to join [[100 Thieves]]. They made the finals in their debut season, with the public seeing them as a middle of the pack team. This resulted in another award for Ssumday, being voted into the 3rd All-Pro Team. In summer, [[100 Thieves]] went through various struggles, with jungler [[Meteos]] leaving the team, and [[Rikara]] eventually stepping into the place of [[Cody Sun]]. Despite that, Ssumday secured the 1st All-Pro Team award and the team managed to place 4th in the season, securing them a slot for [[World_Championship/2018|Worlds 2018]]. [[100 Thieves]] placed 9-12th, only winning against the Taiwanese [[G-Rex]].

In the following seasons, [[100 Thieves]] failed to impress, placing 10th in the [[LCS/2019/Spring|2019 Spring Split]], and after a 1-5 start in the [[LCS/2019/Summer|2019 Summer split]], Ssumday was relegated to the [[100 Thieves Academy]] roster to make space for [[FakeGod]]. This decision was made based on the mid-lane performance, and import regulations wouldn't allow [[Ryu]] to be part of the team without a different import leaving the roster. [[100 Thieves Academy]] managed to win the [[LCS/Academy_League/2019/Summer|2019 Summer academy league]], giving Ssumday his first championship in 5 years as a consolation prize for the rough season. 2020 wasn't much better, but despite a 5-6th and 7-8th placement in the 2020 season, Ssumday was highly regarded as one of the best toplaners in the league.

In 2021, Ssumday was joined by 4 former [[Golden Guardians]] members, they made the semi-finals of [[LCS/2021/Lock_In|2021 Lock-In tournament]], and placed 4th in the [[LCS/2021/Spring|2021 Spring season]] following defeats against [[Cloud9]] and [[TSM]] in playoffs. In Summer, [[100 Thieves]] placed second in the regular season and in the playoffs they beat [[Evil Geniuses]], [[Cloud9]] and eventually [[Team Liquid]] to take the LCS title. This gave Ssumday his first top level title since [[Champions/2014/Summer|Champions 2014 Summer Split]] and making [[100 Thieves]] the 5th ever organization to win the LCS.

their career |fix=add a short history of 1-2 paragraphs with references and hyperlinks (look at established player pages for inspiration) |date=2024-07-11 }} ===LCK Debut With Najin (2015)=== ===Joining The ROX Tigers (2016)=== ===A Year With SKT (2017)=== Ahead of the 2017 season, [[SK Telecom T1]] acquired Peanut from the [[ROX Tigers]] to fill the vacant spot in the jungle Bae "[[Bengi]]" Seong-woong left. {{cite web|url=https://x.com/T1LoL/status/804137025154621440|title=SKT T1의 새로운 정글러를 소개합니다.|trans_title=Introducing SKT T1’s new jungler.|author=[[SK Telecom T1]]|date=2016-12-01|language={{Flag|kr}} Korean}} Together with Peanut together with SKT dominated the season, finishing the regular season with a 16-2 record to place themselves directly in the finals of the Playoffs. Here they defeated [[KT Rolster]] in a 3-0 sweep and qualified for [[Mid-Season_Invitational/2017|MSI]]. At MSI they toppled the Group Stage with a 8-2 record and qualified for the Knockout Stage. Within the Group Stage, peanut had a standout performance playing [[Lee Sin]]. Against their match against the [[GIGABYTE Marines]] Peanut set a recurd for the most kills within the first 15 minutes of a proffesional game. Gaining 15 kills, 12 which were in just the first 12 minutes. {{cite web|url=https://www.redbull.com/us-en/peanut-mvp-mid-season-invitational-red-bull-esports|title=Peanut is our MVP of the Mid Season Invitational|author=Mike Stubbs|publisher=Red Bull|date=2017-05-22|language={{Flag|usuk}} English}} Continuing in the Playoffs they defeated [[Flash Wolves]] in a 3-0 sweep and entered the finals against Europe's [[G2 Esports]]. SK Telecom won the series in a 3-1 victory, with Peanut being awarded the MVP title for the last game. With this victory, Peanut gained his first international trophy. The following split SK Telecom dropped off in performance, only ending in 4th in the regular season. But it seemed the team came back, battling their way through the playoffs to make it back to the finals. They however lost against [[Longzhu Gaming]], but still qualified for [[World_Championship/2017|Worlds]] through the [[LCK/2017/Championship_Points|Championship]] points as the second seed. Meaning Peanut would attend his second World Championship. Now as a part of SKT who had won two World Championship prior. SKT had a strong start in the Group Stage, topping their group. However the Playoffs saw SKT almost lose to [[Misfits Gaming]] as they fell behind 1-2 in the series. SKT however was able to recover and secure the victory. In their next series they found themselves against [[Royal Never Give Up]], which turned into another back-and-forth series, with SKT again coming out on top. Now Peanut has reached his first Worlds Final, however after falling behind in the series 0-2, Peanut was subbed out in favour Kang "[[Blank]]" Sun-gu. The substitution however didn'tt help, as the SKT dominance would end as the team was swept 0-3 by their [[LCK]] counterparts [[Samsung Galaxy]]. Concluding the competitive year, Peanut's contract with SKT had ended and he parted ways with the organization. {{cite web|url=https://x.com/T1LoL/status/932907571714801664|title=2017년 한 해동안 T1에서 활약한 한왕호(Peanut), 김하늘(Sky) 선수가 계약 종료이 되었음을 알려드립니다.|trans_title=We would like to inform you that the contracts of JUNGLE Han-Peanut-wangho and MID Kim-Sky-HANEUL for T1's 2017 season have been expired.|author=[[SK Telecom T1]]|date=2017-11-21|language={{Flag|kr}} Korean}} A few days after it was announced that for the following year, Peanut signed with [[Longzhu Gaming]]. {{cite web|url=https://x.com/kenzi131/status/934443325872005121|title=2Peanut joins .@Longzhu_ #LoL|author=kenzi|date=2017-11-25|language={{Flag|kr}} Korean}} ===Returning to Gen.G (2022)=== ===Last Star of ROX Shine (2024)=== After parting ways with Gen.G, Peanut signed with [[Hanwha Life Esports]], the team that succeeded [[ROX Tigers]]. With his new team, Peanut finished {{Ordinal|3}} in Group Stage of the [[LCK/2024/Spring|Spring Split]], and swept [[Freecs]] 3-0 in the first round of Playoffs. Despite making an upset against [[T1]] with a 3-0 upset, Peanut and his team lost 1-3 to [[Gen.G Esports|Gen.G]] in Upper Bracket Final, then lost 1-3 to [[T1]] in Lower Bracket Final, failing to qualify for the [[Mid-Season Invitational/2024|MSI]]. {{Quote |quote=이런 말이 있거든요. 별의 마지막은 성운을 만들고요, 새로운 세대의 별이 된다고 합니다, 그 1400여년 넘게 자리 지켜온 첨성대 덕분일까요? ROX의 마지막 별이 한화생명 첫 우승으로 빛내는 걸 보게 되네요.
[ There is a saying: the last of a star creates a nebula, which then becomes a star of a new generation. Is it because of [[wikipedia:Cheomseongdae|Cheomseongdae]] that kept its place for about 1400 years? I am seeing the last star of ROX shining with the first championship title of HLE. ] |sign=Jeong "[[NoFe]]" No-chul |source=LCK Summer 2024 Grand Final{{cite web|url=https://youtu.be/C6V2FY0QqwI&t=18826|title=GEN vs HLE {{!}} 결승전 {{!}} 우리은행 2024 LCK 서머 플레이오프|trans_title=GEN vs HLE {{!}} Grand Final {{!}} Woori Bank 2024 LCK Summer Playoffs|publisher=[[LCK]]|language={{FlagNoLink|kr}} Korean|date=2024-09-08}} }} ==Media== {{Player Media}} ==Trivia== * Changed his legal name from Yoon Wang-ho (윤왕호) to Han Wang-ho (한왕호) in April 2016. * Is the first player to have reached 5 [[LCK]] finals in a row - [[LCK/2016/Spring|Spring 2016]] to [[LCK/2018/Spring|Spring 2018]] - doing so with 3 different organizations - [[KOO Tigers]], [[SK Telecom T1]] and [[KING-ZONE DragonX]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Player team roster}}
